subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write briefly about different waves and intervals in an ECG.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.44, SAQ 47. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Figure revision (figure audit, 2026-09-05): a second heartbeat was added so the R-R interval named in the answer can be marked, and the P-R and Q-T brackets now start where the card defines them. Revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the insider note no longer says the durations are the marks, since the fourth mark is the labelled trace, and the T wave step's WHY now states that the T wave is ventricular repolarisation, which the printed line does not say.

steps.label: P wave and QRS complex
steps.why: Each wave is the electrical signal that makes a chamber contract, so the trace is a record of the cardiac cycle.
common_mistakes: Giving the P wave to the ventricles. It is atrial systole.
Leaving out the three parts of the QRS complex.
steps.memory_tip: P for atria, QRS for ventricles, T for recovery.
steps.margin_note: Give a duration with every wave.
lines: ECG stands for electrocardiograph. It
records electrical changes in the heart.
Twelve sensors are placed at 12 places and
the leads are connected to the machine.
P wave represents atrial systole. Its
duration is 0.1 s.
QRS complex represents ventricular systole.
Its duration is 0.08 to 0.1 s.
Q is a small negative wave, R is a tall
positive wave and S is a small negative
wave.

steps.label: T wave
steps.why: The T wave represents repolarisation, the electrical recovery of the ventricles after they contract, and the end of the T wave marks the end of ventricular systole.
common_mistakes: Giving the T wave to atrial recovery.
steps.memory_tip: T is the ventricles recovering, 0.2 s.

steps.label: The three intervals
steps.why: An interval measures the time between two events, so it shows how fast the signal travels through the heart.
common_mistakes: Confusing the QT interval with the QRS complex.
Leaving out that R-R is one whole cardiac cycle.
steps.memory_tip: PR 0.12-0.2 s, QT 0.4 s, RR 0.8 s — one full beat.
steps.margin_note: Three intervals, each with its duration.
lines: P-R interval is the time between the onset
of the P wave and the onset of the Q wave.
Its duration is 0.12 to 0.2 s.
Q-T interval is between the onset of the Q
wave and the end of the T wave. It depends
on heart rate and lasts about 0.4 s. If the
heart beats faster the interval is shorter.
R-R interval is the duration of one cardiac
cycle. Its duration is 0.8 s.

steps.label: Diagram — a normal ECG
steps.why: The trace shows the waves in the order they occur, which is exactly what makes the intervals easy to read off.
common_mistakes: Drawing the R wave downward. It is the tall positive spike.
steps.memory_tip: Small bump, tall spike, second bump: P, QRS, T.
steps.margin_note: Mark the intervals under the trace with brackets.
